appraisal_events.evidence: Gilberte writes to the narrator on a different letterhead each time 'parce que j'étais une relation encore assez nouvelle,' invites him to her goûters, checks whether he is hungry, and makes him tea, extracting for him a whole section of the chocolate cake.
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte's individualized, solicitous hospitality marks the narrator as a specially attended-to guest inside her intimate world, deepening his favored position within her household.

appraisal_events.evidence: The narrator tells his parents the staircase was an antique piece brought from afar by M. Swann; his father flatly corrects him (it is an ordinary Berlier-built building), yet the narrator 'écartai à tout jamais' the deflating thought, comparing himself to a devout believer refusing rationalist criticism of scripture.
appraisal_events.explanation: The mature narrator ironically exposes his younger self's credulous, self-serving fabrication and willful refusal of plain fact in order to protect the Swanns' imagined prestige and his own happiness.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator gains a modest emotional advantage in being personally and attentively cared for by Gilberte within the private ritual of her goûters.
The retrospective narrator's ironic self-portrait exposes his younger self as credulous and self-deceiving, mildly diminishing him even as the passage treats this with affectionate humor.
